propositions: CLI `--output json` emits nanosecond timestamps as bare 19-digit JSON numbers exceeding 2**53-1, causing silent float64 rounding (~42ns drift) in jq/Node/Ruby and BigInt serialization failures in strict consumers

All CLI store-data `--output json` and `--output llm` emitters now route through `js_safe_dumps`, converting out-of-JS-safe-range integers to exact decimal strings while preserving in-range values unchanged

An AST guard `scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py` wired into `make lint` fails if a CLI emitter writes store data through raw `json.dumps` without js-safe conversion, preventing silent reintroduction of the defect
The conversion is lossless for consumers coercing with `int()`/`BigInt()` and the wire format no longer silently rounds nanosecond precision
The plain-dict serialization path (no pydantic `model_validate` round-trip) preserves the decimal-string wire form, and schemas already type these fields as `['integer','string','null']`
